concepts.name: Database Transactions
concepts.description: Grouping several SQL statements into one atomic unit that either fully commits or fully rolls back, so a failure never leaves partial changes.
concepts.context: transfer() in app/transfers.py wraps the balance check, both UPDATEs and the ledger INSERT in `with conn:` so an exception rolls back every write

concepts.name: Connection Context Manager
concepts.description: Python's sqlite3 connection used as a context manager commits on clean exit and rolls back on exception, but does not close the connection.
concepts.context: `with conn:` in app/transfers.py:2 replaces manual commit/rollback; raising InsufficientFunds inside the block triggers the rollback

concepts.name: Check-Then-Act Race
concepts.description: A race where a value is read and checked, then written based on that check, while another writer can change it in between, so the check no longer holds.
concepts.context: transfer() in app/transfers.py reads the balance with SELECT then compares to cents before the UPDATE, so two concurrent transfers can both pass the check and overdraw the account

concepts.name: Parameterized Queries
concepts.description: Passing SQL values as bound parameters instead of string-formatting them into the query, which prevents SQL injection and handles quoting.
concepts.context: Every statement in app/transfers.py uses `?` placeholders with a tuple, e.g. `WHERE id = ?` with `(src,)`, so src, dst and cents are never interpolated

concepts.name: Domain Exceptions
concepts.description: Raising a specific custom exception to signal a business-rule failure and abort the current operation, letting callers handle it by type.
concepts.context: transfer() raises InsufficientFunds(src) in app/transfers.py:4 when the balance is below cents, which also triggers the transaction rollback

concepts.name: Ledger Audit Trail
concepts.description: Recording every money movement as an append-only row in a ledger table in the same transaction as the balance change, so balances and history cannot diverge.
concepts.context: The INSERT INTO ledger (src, dst, cents) in app/transfers.py:8 sits inside the same `with conn:` block as the two balance UPDATEs, so a rollback also drops the ledger row

concepts.name: Atomic SQL Update
concepts.description: Updating a value relative to its current value inside the statement (balance = balance - ?) so the database applies it atomically instead of the app writing back a stale read.
concepts.context: The two UPDATEs in app/transfers.py:6-7 use `balance = balance - ?` and `balance + ?` rather than writing a computed value from the earlier SELECT

concepts.name: Database Transaction
concepts.description: A group of SQL statements that commit together or roll back together, so a failure part-way leaves no partial change.
concepts.context: `with conn:` in transfer() in app/transfers.py commits the debit, credit and ledger insert together, and rolls all three back if InsufficientFunds or any statement raises

concepts.name: Context Manager
concepts.description: A `with` block that runs setup and cleanup code around its body, including when the body raises an exception.
concepts.context: sqlite3's connection works as a context manager in transfer(): leaving the `with conn:` block normally commits, and leaving it on an exception rolls back. It does not close the connection

concepts.name: Check-Then-Act Race
concepts.description: A bug where a condition is read and then acted on in separate steps, so another writer can change the value in between and make the check stale.
concepts.context: transfer() reads the balance with SELECT and checks `row[0] < cents` before the UPDATE. A concurrent transfer from the same account can pass the same check, so the balance can go negative

concepts.name: SQL Parameterization
concepts.description: Passing values to a query as bound parameters (`?` placeholders) instead of building the SQL string, so input cannot change the query.
concepts.context: Every statement in transfer() binds src, dst and cents through `?` placeholders with a tuple, so a hostile account id cannot inject SQL

concepts.name: Atomic Update
concepts.description: Letting the database compute a new value from the old one in a single statement, such as `balance = balance - ?`, instead of reading it into the application, changing it and writing it back.
concepts.context: The two UPDATE statements in transfer() use `balance = balance - ?` and `balance = balance + ?`, so no stale value from the earlier SELECT gets written back

concepts.name: Ledger Audit Trail
concepts.description: An append-only record of each money movement, written in the same transaction as the balance change, so balances and history cannot disagree.
concepts.context: The INSERT INTO ledger (src, dst, cents) in transfer() commits atomically with the two balance updates, so a recorded transfer always has matching balance changes

concepts.name: Exception-Driven Rollback
concepts.description: Raising a domain exception to abort a unit of work, so the surrounding transaction discards everything done so far.
concepts.context: `raise InsufficientFunds(src)` inside the `with conn:` block in transfer() leaves the block through the exception, which makes the connection roll back before the error reaches the caller
